TPI LUX / service 01

Architectural and landscape lighting

We design, supply and install lighting systems for facades, parks, public spaces and private grounds. The lighting is matched to the architecture, to how the site is run and to its budget.

Discuss a project See scope of work
The TPI LUX principle Lighting chosen for the site, not for the warehouse

Equipment is chosen for the site, not for what happens to be in stock: the task, the environment, service life and budget matter more than one-size-fits-all solutions.

Scope of work

What this service covers

The outline is drawn from working material and presented here in the format of a commercial page.

Lighting concept development

The overall lighting idea, accounting for the architecture, the surroundings, usage scenarios and the visual result.

Design and calculations

Lighting calculations, equipment layout drawings, cable routes and design documentation.

Equipment selection and supply

Architectural floodlights, linear luminaires, contour lighting and accent solutions for the specific site.

Installation and connection

Cable laying, equipment mounting, connection and testing of the system before commissioning.

Scene programming

Static and dynamic modes, accent scenes and integration with lighting control systems.

Maintenance

Support after commissioning: diagnostics, servicing, replacement of components and monitoring of stable operation.

Solutions

Typical project components

  • linear facade luminaires
  • architectural floodlights
  • contour lighting
  • accent luminaires
  • garden and park luminaires
  • in-ground luminaires
  • pathway lighting
  • decorative lighting elements
Engineering accountability

Why TPI LUX

A complete approach to the project: concept, design, procurement, installation, commissioning and maintenance under a single responsibility.

The team works on large sites where deadlines, safety, quality control and clear communication matter.

Solutions are chosen for the site and for how it will be run, not only for how it looks on day one.

Enquiry
